title: Adaptive slice suballocator with tiered spill hysteresis and compact-on-evict
author: Ethan Park
description: Context: The KV cache has increasingly suffered from micro-fragmentation under mixed-length workloads (short response KV entries interleaved with large context blobs). This causes premature spills and paging which degrades tail latency. Motivation: introduce a lightweight, adaptive suballocator that reduces internal fragmentation, coordinate compaction with eviction to avoid double-copy churn, and add a tiered spill hysteresis to dampen oscillatory spill/reload cycles. Summary of changes: 1) New adaptive slice suballocator (pkg/kv/suballocator.go) that splits large slabs into variable 'slices' sized by observed allocation-size histogram and runtime fragmentation score. The suballocator supports fast-path allocation for hot-size buckets and a fallback coalescing slow-path for large sparse allocations. 2) Compact-on-evict policy: when an eviction candidate is selected, the allocator attempts an in-place compact if the tenant's fragmentation score is above a configured threshold; this reduces downstream spill volume. 3) Tiered spill hysteresis: spill thresholds now use a three-level hysteresis (soft/warm/hard) per-tenant and are backed by a moving-average resident-set and OS page-fault signal to prevent oscillation during bursty traffic. 4) OS-paging-aware backpressure: runtime signals (page-fault rate and swap utilization) feed into the spill controller to throttle batching aggressiveness and avoid cascading IO. 5) Background compactor: asynchronous compaction runs with an IO budget aware rate limiter that cooperates with the scheduler to yield during high-batching windows. 6) Telemetry and runtime knobs: new metrics (kv.slice_size_distribution, kv.fragmentation_score, kv.compaction_cycles, kv.spill_hysteresis_state) and configuration flags (kv.slice_min, kv.slice_max, kv.compact_eviction_threshold, kv.spill_warm_ratio). Checklists: - [x] Implement adaptive slice suballocator - [x] Add compact-on-evict path and unit tests - [x] Implement tiered spill hysteresis and OS signal integration - [x] Add telemetry and knobs - [x] Benchmarks and microbench harness added - [x] E2E perf validation against stress harness (bench/kv/sim_bench.go) Perf summary: Microbench on p4d and internal GPU clusters shows 18-26% reduction in mean eviction-induced spill bytes and a 12% improvement in 95th percentile tail TTFB for mixed small/large workloads. Under sustained large-blob workloads the soft-warm tiers reduce unnecessary full spills by ~40%, lowering datastore IO. Risk: Compaction can add CPU overhead; the compact-on-evict path is gated behind per-tenant thresholds and an adaptive sampling rate. Related: builds on earlier KV residency and eviction work; coordinates with scheduler changes in runtime/evictor to ensure compaction doesn't collide with token-critical batches. Links: Linear ENG-2345 design doc internal link (design/redwood/kv/adaptive-slice-suballoc), incident SUP-4211 notes for previous paging spike.

review_comments: Maya Chen: Nit - can we move histogram sampling into a pluggable tracer so experiments don't touch core path? Also please add a flamegraph on compaction CPU cost.
Author (Ethan Park): Moved sampling to a lightweight interface and added a feature flag; attached flamegraphs from benchmark runs in a follow-up commit.
Noah Alvarez: The spill hysteresis looks sensible, but I'm worried about tenant fairness when warm->hard transitions occur. Suggest adding a tenant_pacing window metric so we can detect starvation.
Author (Ethan Park): Added tenant.pacing_window metric and adjusted the scheduler to consider pacing when selecting eviction candidates.
Priya Natarajan: Tests look good; can we add a short e2e stress that asserts no increase in page-fault rate after enabling the feature?
Author (Ethan Park): Added sim_bench scenario that asserts page-fault rate stays below configured threshold under mixed workload.
release_notes: Introduce adaptive slice suballocator to reduce KV cache fragmentation, compact-on-evict to reduce spill volume, and tiered spill hysteresis to stabilize spill behavior under bursty traffic. Adds observability metrics and tuning knobs. Backwards compatible; feature gated by kv.slice_min > 0 flag.
